sources.citation: AIATSIS Collections (comp. Lisa Marcussen). 2014. Selected bibliography of material on the Bayali / Baiali language and people held in the AIATSIS Library. 13 pp.
sources.note: Bibliography only. Language-tagged items are Curr 1887 no. 160 (wordlist) and Terrill 1993 Biri BA(Hons) thesis (AIATSIS MS 3262, which 'surveys.. neighbouring languages' incl. Bayali); everything else is ethnographic/people-tagged.

sources.citation: Ulm, Sean. 2006. Coastal Themes: An Archaeology of the Southern Curtis Coast, Queensland. Terra Australis 24. Canberra: ANU E Press. (Ch. 2 'The study region', 'Cultural setting', pp. 22-23.)
sources.note: Nothing; no language data at all. Relevant only to the identity of Curr no. 162 (Meerooni) -- Gooreng Gooreng, not Bayali.

sources.citation: Terrill, Angela. 2002. Dharumbal: the language of Rockhampton, Australia. Pacific Linguistics 525. Canberra: Australian National University. xii+108 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5009.5.R63 T47 2002)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5009.5.R63 T47 2002
sources.note: About Bayali (sec. 2.3, p. 15): 'There is very little information on Bayali; the only extant linguistic information comes from one word list in Curr's compilation (Anon 1886).' Its own stress section (sec. 3.6, p. 24) is about DHARUMBAL (dhar1248), not Bayali: 'Stress is usually, but not always, on the first syllable of a word.. It is not clear from the written sources whether or not stress was phonemic'.

sources.citation: Mathew, John. 1914. Note on the Gurang Gurang tribe of Queensland, with vocabulary. Report of the Fourteenth Meeting of the Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science (Melbourne, 1913), 433-443.
sources.note: Nothing on Bayali; the paper's vocabulary and remarks are Gurang Gurang only (not examined for Gurang Gurang stress here, out of scope).

sources.citation: Anonymous. 1887. No. 160: Keppel Bay, Calliope River, and Curtis Island [Byellee tribe]. In E. M. Curr (ed.), The Australian Race, vol. 3, pp. 114-115. Melbourne: John Ferres, Government Printer.
sources.note: The only primary linguistic record of Bayali: a bare ~100-item wordlist with a short ethnographic preamble; no accent marks, no remark on accent or stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Bayali language' (wikitext via API, 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing; pointers to Glottolog, Dixon 2002:xxxiv, SLQ word map, AIATSIS bibliography, and the Central Queensland Language Centre revival project (since 2017).

sources.citation: AIATSIS Austlang record E42: Baiali (Internet Archive copy 2024-12-08; live site could not be reached by automated download).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Comment: 'The data for this language are scarce; there is a word list in Curr for Byellee (E42) (1887: 114-115).' Documentation scores: Word list <20 pages = 1; Grammar = None; Text = None; Audio-visual = None. Bowern p.c. 2021: sister to Gooreng-Gooreng (Waka-Kabi) on the Curr list.

sources.citation: Breen, Gavan (2009). The Biri Dialects and their Neighbours. Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 133(2): 219-256. DOI 10.1080/03721426.2009.10887121
sources.note: nothing: the article is a review of dialect names, territories and old wordlist sources; it contains no phonological or prosodic statement for Bayali (or for any language -- no occurrence of stress/accent/tone/syllable in the text apart from a remark on a diacritic in a manuscript).

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois & Geraldine Triffitt. 1999. OZBIB: a linguistic bibliography of Aboriginal Australia and the Torres Strait Islands. Pacific Linguistics D-92. Canberra: ANU. (Language index 'Bayali: Anonymous 1887, Commissioner 1887'.)
sources.note: no phonology content (bibliography); documents that as of 1999 no description of Bayali existed beyond two 1887 wordlists.

sources.citation: Holmer, Nils M. 1983. Linguistic survey of south-eastern Queensland. Pacific Linguistics D-54. Canberra: Australian National University. viii+492 pp.
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7091.Q4 H65 1983
sources.note: Contains NO Bayali section (the earlier scan's 'pp. 469-478 Bayali section' does not exist; TOC and text checked, no Bayali/Byellee/Orambul anywhere). pp. 456-478 are the DARUMBAL chapter (Great/North Keppel Island informant = Wapabara Dharumbal per Terrill 2002:13-14); sec. 17.4 p. 457: 'Although stress is not distinctive in Darumbal, the usual tendency toward stressing of the second initial syllable in long words or sequences prevails'.

sources.citation: Oates, Lynette F. 1975. The 1973 supplement to A revised linguistic survey of Australia. Armidale: Christian Book Centre. p. 219, entry 96.1c 'Bayali, Keppel Island, E4 (AIAS E42)'. (AIATSIS Austlang sheet.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: survey line with names, status 'Extinct', two words for 'man' and source code C:160 (Curr no. 160).

sources.citation: Schmidt, Wilhelm. 1914. Die Gliederung der australischen Sprachen [part]. Anthropos 9: 980-1018 (section 'VIII. Das Bieli', p. 988; 'E. Nord-Kabi' p. 988; 'Zum Bieli und Kuinmurburra' p. ~996). (Book edition: Schmidt 1919, Die Gliederung der australischen Sprachen, Wien: Mechitharisten.)
sources.note: No phonology of Bieli at all; the only sound-related remark in the surrounding pages is the distribution of word-final -m across the East-coast group. Lexical comparison only (numerals, 'fire', etc.).

sources.citation: Lauterer, Joseph. 1897. Aboriginal languages of Eastern Australia compared [a philological essay; read 6 March 1896]. Proceedings of the Royal Society of Queensland 12: 11-16. (AIATSIS p LAU; language-tagged Bayali/Baiali E42 in the AIATSIS 2014 bibliography.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or any phonology of Byellee; the essay compares negatives and a few lexemes (foot, camp, father) across Eastern Australia using Curr.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record baya1257 Bayali (and subgroup rock1234 Rockhampton-Gladstone = Bayali + Dharumbal dhar1248).
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's most extensive descriptions listed: Besold 2012 (ANU PhD on NSW South Coast languages -- a mis-assignment, not about Bayali) and 'Commissioner of Police, Brisbane 1887' = the Curr wordlist (2 pp.).

sources.citation: Roth, Walter E. 1898. The Aborigines of the Rockhampton and surrounding coast districts. Manuscript report to the Commissioner of Police, Queensland (Mitchell Library, State Library of NSW, Sydney).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Roth lists Oorumbal (= Bayali per Terrill 2002:13) among the district's tribes and, per Terrill 2002:24, hyphenates syllables and underlines the stressed syllable in his wordlists; if any Oorumbal/Urambal items exist there they would be the only stress-marked Bayali data (Terrill implies none survive, so low odds).

sources.citation: Besold, Jutta. 2012. Language Recovery of the New South Wales South Coast Aboriginal Languages. PhD thesis, Australian National University. (Glottolog's sole 'grammar sketch' ref for baya1257)
